headline: Daily market snapshot — September 1 2026
summary: Closing market levels for September 1 2026: equities fell on renewed Iran-US hostilities and higher energy prices; 10Y yield rose to 4.75%; WTI at $86.57 and Brent at $91.28; DXY ~99.6; BTC ~$78,539.

headline: Two oil tankers hit by projectiles in Strait of Hormuz overnight — one Saudi, one South Korean-owned
summary: Two supertankers carrying Saudi crude were struck by projectiles within minutes of each other in the Strait of Hormuz overnight Monday-Tuesday. The incident, linked to renewed US-Iran hostilities, lifted oil prices roughly 2% and deepened fears about supply disruptions at the world's most critical oil chokepoint.
key_facts: Two supertankers each loaded 2 million barrels of Saudi crude struck near-simultaneously
UK Maritime Trade Operations reported three projectiles hitting one tanker
Incident attributed to Iranian forces in context of US-Iran war since Feb 28 2026
Oil prices rose ~2% on the news

headline: Dow futures fall 240 points to kick off September as oil and yields surge
summary: US equity futures slid at the September open: Dow futures -240 pts (-0.5%), S&P 500 futures -0.5%, Nasdaq-100 futures nearly -1%, as surging crude prices and rising Treasury yields weighed on risk appetite following overnight tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts: Oil surge and rising yields cited as main drivers
Tanker attacks in Hormuz overnight amplified risk-off

headline: Stock market today: Dow -374, S&P -0.3%, Nasdaq -0.1% as inflation and Fed rate-hike fears persist
summary: US stocks finished lower September 1, with the Dow shedding 374 points (-0.7%) to 53,185.90, the S&P 500 falling 0.3% to 7,686.14, and the Nasdaq dipping 0.1% to 26,370.89. Elevated oil prices from Hormuz tensions, the 10-year yield at 4.75%, and Fed rate-hike expectations combined to pressure equities.

headline: WTI crude rises to $86.57 and Brent to $91.28 on Hormuz tanker attacks
summary: WTI crude climbed to $86.57/bbl (+0.94%) and Brent to $91.28/bbl (+0.87%) on September 1, as tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz renewed supply-disruption fears. Oil is up 7.75% (WTI) and 8.96% (Brent) over the past month, and roughly 32% year-over-year, driven by the Iran war.
key_facts: Tanker attacks overnight renewed supply fears

headline: Asian LNG climbs to five-month high at $24.614/MMBtu on Hormuz disruption fears
summary: Asian spot LNG prices rose to $24.614/MMBtu, a five-month high, as Strait of Hormuz disruptions from the US-Iran war raised fears of prolonged LNG supply constraints. Roughly 20% of global LNG transits the strait, primarily from Qatar, and flows have been severely curtailed since March 2026.
key_facts: ~20% of global LNG transits Strait of Hormuz
QatarEnergy declared force majeure in March 2026
Analysts expect LNG prices above $18-20/MMBtu through end of 2026
TTF European natural gas also surging

headline: Warsh hawkish Jackson Hole speech pushes September rate-hike odds to 57-60%
summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's August 28 Jackson Hole keynote — warning that summer's better inflation readings do not confirm underlying improvement and reaffirming the 2% target — drove markets to price a 57-60% probability of a 25 bps hike at the September 15-16 FOMC, up from ~40% the week prior. Warsh's stance puts the Fed at odds with Trump's calls for lower rates.
key_facts: CME FedWatch: 60.4% chance of 25 bps Sept hike
Warsh: summer inflation data do not confirm underlying improvement
Speech seen reinforcing Fed independence against fiscal pressure
Three FOMC members (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) already dissented at July meeting

headline: FOMC meeting September 15-16 with rate decision at 2 PM ET on September 16
summary: The next Federal Open Market Committee meeting is scheduled for September 15-16, 2026, with the policy statement and press conference on September 16 at 2:00 PM ET. Markets currently price 57-60% probability of a 25 bps rate hike to 3.75-4.0%; a Summary of Economic Projections (dot plot) will also be released.
key_facts: Market odds: 57-60% for 25 bps hike to 3.75-4.0%

headline: JOLTS July 2026: 7.36 million job openings, missing 7.40 million consensus
summary: The BLS released the July 2026 JOLTS report on September 1, showing 7.36 million job openings, slightly below the 7.40 million consensus estimate and the prior reading of ~7.36 million. The modest miss suggests labor demand is gently cooling, potentially softening the case for an aggressive September Fed rate hike.
key_facts: Modest cooling may temper urgency for Sept rate hike

headline: ISM Manufacturing PMI August 2026 consensus 55.2; S&P Global Mfg PMI at 53.2
summary: The ISM Manufacturing PMI for August 2026 was released September 1 with a consensus forecast of 55.2 (prior 55.6), alongside the S&P Global Manufacturing PMI at 53.2 (prior 53.9 in July). Higher fuel costs, reduced inventory building, and raw-material shortages linked to Hormuz supply delays weighed on activity. Both readings remain above 50, indicating expansion.
key_facts: ISM Manufacturing PMI Aug forecast 55.2, prior 55.6
S&P Global Mfg PMI Aug: 53.2, prior 53.9
Higher fuel costs and Hormuz-related supply delays weighed
Manufacturing employment rose modestly at fastest pace since May

headline: US 10-year Treasury yield rises to 4.75% as September rate-hike bets build
summary: The 10-year US Treasury yield rose to 4.75% on September 1, 2026, driven by growing expectations of a Fed rate hike at the September 15-16 FOMC following Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech. Both oil-price-driven inflation fears and tighter monetary policy expectations pushed long yields higher.
key_facts: Rate hike odds ~57-60% for September FOMC
Oil-driven inflation fears add upward pressure on long yields

headline: Nikkei 225 falls 0.6% below 66,000 as oil inflation fears pressure Japan equities
summary: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 0.6% to below 66,000 on September 1, extending prior-session losses as higher oil prices stoked inflation concerns and heightened near-term Fed rate-hike expectations. A weak Wall Street lead and climbing Treasury yields added to the downward pressure.
key_facts: Oil-driven inflation and Fed hike bets the key drivers
Tech and AI-related stocks led declines

headline: Asia-Pacific stocks broadly lower Tuesday as Hormuz tanker attacks renew supply fears
summary: Markets in Australia, Japan, South Korea, China, and Hong Kong all fell September 1, 2026, as overnight Hormuz tanker attacks raised energy-supply concerns and oil climbed higher. Technology and AI-related shares led regional declines, tracking the weak US close.
key_facts: Australia, Japan, South Korea, China, Hong Kong all lower
Oil surge stoked inflation and rate-hike concerns
Tech and AI shares led Asia-Pacific losses
Region tracked weak Wall Street lead

headline: European markets pause at start of September; CAC 40 +0.4% to ~8,367
summary: European equities were cautiously mixed on September 1 as investors returned from summer break. The CAC 40 rose 0.4% to around 8,367 while investors awaited ECB guidance and Eurozone inflation data. The Stoxx 50 gained 2% in August and Stoxx 600 +0.9%, with the DAX hitting record highs during the prior month.
key_facts: Stoxx 50 +2% in August; Stoxx 600 +0.9% in August
DAX hit record highs in August
Investors await ECB meeting and Eurozone inflation data in Sept

headline: Sibanye-Stillwater H1 2026 HEPS 571-631 cents vs 190 cents prior year on gold and PGM surge
summary: Sibanye-Stillwater (SBSW) reported H1 2026 headline EPS of 571-631 cents (vs. 190c H1 2025) and basic EPS of 597-658 cents (vs. a loss of 127c in H1 2025), driven by a 35% rise in the rand gold price, 5% higher gold sold, and improved PGM margins. Results were released before the US open on September 1.

headline: Sibanye-Stillwater outperforms premarket on Citi upgrade with $5,000/oz gold target by year-end
summary: Sibanye-Stillwater (SBSW) was outperforming peers in premarket trading September 1, boosted by a Citi analyst upgrade citing bullish revisions forecasting gold prices to reach $5,000 per troy ounce by year-end 2026, alongside the release of strong H1 2026 earnings results.
key_facts: Citi upgraded SBSW with $5,000/oz gold year-end target
Dual catalysts: analyst upgrade and strong H1 2026 earnings

headline: Broadcom Q3 FY2026 earnings September 2: consensus revenue $29.43B, GAAP EPS $2.55
summary: Broadcom reports fiscal Q3 2026 results September 2, with consensus revenue of $29.43B and GAAP EPS of $2.55. The company guided Q3 revenue at ~$29.4B with non-GAAP operating margin ~67% and adjusted EBITDA ~68%. AI semiconductor revenue grew 143% YoY to $10.8B in Q2 FY2026, accounting for nearly half of total revenue.
key_facts: Q3 FY2026 earnings due Sept 2 after close

headline: Micron Q4 FY2026 earnings September 30: analysts target $50.8B revenue, $31.28 EPS
summary: Micron Technology reports fiscal Q4 2026 results September 30, with analyst consensus of $50.8B revenue (+348% YoY) and EPS of $31.28 (10x+ YoY). Q3 FY2026 already showed $41.5B revenue and 85% gross margin. High-bandwidth memory for AI servers is the primary demand driver; MU is up ~228% YTD.
key_facts: Q3 FY2026 revenue: $41.5B, gross margin 85%, net income $28.2B
HBM for AI servers primary driver; HBM needs ~4x wafer capacity vs standard DRAM

headline: Semiconductor ETF up ~70% YTD in 2026 as chipmakers outshine Big Tech in AI rally
summary: A popular semiconductor ETF has surged approximately 70% year to date in 2026, with chipmakers outperforming traditional Big Tech as the primary AI infrastructure beneficiaries. Broadcom (Sept 2 earnings) and Micron (Sept 30 earnings) are the next major catalysts on the AI hardware calendar in September.
key_facts: Chipmakers outperforming Big Tech in AI cycle
NVDA +~9% post Q2 FY27 earnings; revenue doubled YoY
Broadcom Q3 (Sept 2) and Micron Q4 (Sept 30) are next catalysts
Google eyeing $190B AI capex buildout supporting chip demand

headline: Google eyes $190 billion AI infrastructure buildout, lifting semiconductor demand outlook
summary: Reports indicate Google/Alphabet is planning a $190 billion AI infrastructure buildout, among the largest corporate capex programs in history, which would directly benefit semiconductor companies supplying AI accelerators, HBM memory, and networking chips. Analysts see the announcement as a structural tailwind for the sector through 2027.
key_facts: One of largest single corporate capex programs in history
Direct beneficiaries: NVDA, AVGO, MU, AMD
Supports semiconductor demand for rest of 2026 into 2027

headline: NVIDIA shares climbed ~9% post Q2 FY2027 earnings as revenue roughly doubled year-over-year
summary: NVIDIA's stock climbed approximately 9% following its Q2 FY2027 earnings release (late August 2026), in which the company reported revenue of approximately $96.2B, roughly doubling year-over-year. The results reaffirmed NVIDIA's dominance in AI accelerators and boosted the broader semiconductor sector.
key_facts: Q2 FY2027 revenue ~$96.2B, roughly doubled YoY

headline: Morgan Stanley raises TeraWulf price target to $72 from $66.50, Overweight
summary: Morgan Stanley raised the price target on TeraWulf (WULF) to $72 from $66.50, maintaining an Overweight rating, citing the company's strategic pivot to AI and high-performance computing infrastructure anchored by a 20-year Anthropic lease at its Justified Data campus generating ~$19B in contracted revenue.

20-year Anthropic AI/HPC lease at Justified Data campus
Contracted revenue from Anthropic deal est. ~$19B

summary: Piper Sandler analyst David Westenberg upgraded Neogen (NEOG) from Neutral to Overweight and raised the price target to $14 from $13, reflecting a more constructive view on the food and animal safety testing company's near-term prospects.
key_facts: NEOG upgraded Neutral → Overweight at Piper Sandler

headline: Piper Sandler downgrades Trupanion to Neutral, cuts price target to $32 from $45
summary: Piper Sandler analyst David Westenberg downgraded Trupanion (TRUP) from Overweight to Neutral and sharply cut the price target to $32 from $45, signaling a deteriorating near-term outlook for the pet insurance company.
key_facts: TRUP downgraded Overweight → Neutral at Piper Sandler

headline: UBS cuts ConocoPhillips price target to $143 from $155, maintains Buy
summary: UBS analyst Josh Silverstein maintained a Buy rating on ConocoPhillips (COP) while lowering the price target to $143 from $155, reflecting moderated near-term assumptions despite higher oil prices from the Strait of Hormuz supply crunch.

headline: Scotiabank raises SentinelOne price target to $26 from $23.50 on AI security momentum
summary: Scotiabank analyst Patrick Colville maintained a Sector Outperform rating on SentinelOne (S) and raised the price target to $26 from $23.50, citing strong momentum in AI-driven cybersecurity solutions.

headline: UBS cuts Constellium price target to $35 from $38, maintains Buy
summary: UBS analyst Alex Stansbury maintained a Buy rating on Constellium (CSTM) while lowering the price target to $35 from $38, reflecting moderated near-term expectations for the aluminum products company.

headline: Defense stocks rally on US-Iran conflict: Northrop Grumman +6%, RTX +5%
summary: US defense stocks continued to outperform amid the prolonged Iran conflict, with Northrop Grumman gaining approximately 6% on stealth-bomber and missile-defense demand, RTX rising ~5%, with L3Harris and General Dynamics also posting gains. Defense budgets in the US and Europe face fewer political hurdles due to the ongoing hostilities.
key_facts: L3Harris and General Dynamics also gained
Defense sector benefiting from Iran war conflict and budget tailwinds
US and European defense budgets face fewer political hurdles in 2026

headline: Energy sector outperforms: up 37% in Q1 2026 on Iran-driven oil surge; OXY, COP, CVX, XOM favored
summary: US energy stocks have been the standout sector of 2026, rising approximately 37% in Q1 alone driven by the Iran war-linked oil price surge. Analysts continue to favor ExxonMobil, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, Occidental Petroleum, Enbridge, and Cheniere Energy for their exposure to elevated crude prices and LNG export opportunities.
key_facts: OXY, COP, CVX, XOM, Cheniere, Enbridge highlighted
Sector benefiting from Iran-war supply crunch and sustained elevated oil prices

headline: Bitcoin at $78,539 and Ethereum at $2,479 as Fed rate-hike expectations pressure crypto
summary: Bitcoin traded at approximately $78,539 and Ethereum at $2,479 on September 1, 2026, with both assets under modest pressure from rising Fed rate-hike expectations following Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks. BTC is near the estimated $78K production cost for Bitcoin miners, squeezing profitability for the sector.
key_facts: Higher rate expectations weighing on risk/speculative assets
Bitcoin near ~$78K estimated production cost for miners
TeraWulf pivoting away from mining toward AI/HPC

headline: DXY at ~99.6; USD/JPY 159.75 as dollar supported by Fed rate-hike bets
summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY) traded around 99.6 on September 1, 2026, supported by Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations but capped by geopolitical uncertainty. USD/JPY held at 159.75, with the yen down 1.63% versus the dollar over the past month and 7.52% over the past year.
key_facts: Dollar supported by September rate-hike bets (~60%)

summary: Gold traded at approximately $4,450.95 per troy ounce as of late August/September 1, 2026, having pulled back from the all-time-high area near $4,647 following Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech that boosted rate-hike expectations. Gold remains up 9.76% over the past month and 28.02% YoY; Citi forecasts $5,000/oz by year-end.
key_facts: Pulled back from ~$4,647 ATH area after Warsh speech
Iran tensions and geopolitics support long-term floor

headline: Technology XLK -1.6% and utilities XLU -1% lead sector declines on September 1
summary: The Information Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK) fell 1.6% and utilities (XLU) declined 1% on September 1, 2026, as rising Treasury yields, Fed rate-hike expectations, and oil-driven inflation pressured rate-sensitive and growth-oriented sectors disproportionately.

Analysts warn of underpriced risk heading into Sept

headline: Hormuz shipping traffic down 95%; Gulf crude exports halved since Feb 2026 Iran war onset
summary: Since US-Israeli strikes on Iran began February 28, 2026, traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped approximately 95%. Gulf crude exports fell from ~17M bpd in 2025 to ~9M bpd by August 2026, with direct Hormuz crude flows at 2.2M bpd. The IEA has called it the largest oil supply disruption in market history; Brent surged past $120 at peak.
key_facts: IEA: largest supply disruption in oil market history
Brent surged past $120/bbl at March 2026 peak
QatarEnergy declared force majeure on all exports March 2026

headline: European TTF natural gas surges on Hormuz LNG risks; US gas +4%
summary: European TTF natural gas prices surged as Iran-US hostilities and Strait of Hormuz disruptions raised fears of prolonged LNG supply constraints. US natural gas prices rose more than 4%. Analysts expect LNG supply constraints through end of 2026 and Q1 2027 based on the ongoing Hormuz crisis.
key_facts: European TTF natural gas surging on Iran/Hormuz tensions
~20% of global LNG transits Strait of Hormuz
Supply constraint expected through Q1 2027 per analyst base case

headline: Three FOMC hawks dissented at July meeting, calling for immediate 25 bps rate hike
summary: The Federal Reserve left rates unchanged at 3.5-3.75% at its July 29 meeting with an unusual 9-3 vote, with FOMC members Beth Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie Logan dissenting in favor of an immediate 25 bps hike. The three dissenters have grown increasingly vocal about the need to contain inflation, raising pressure ahead of the September 15-16 meeting.

Dissenters: Hammack, Kashkari, Logan — all favored 25 bps hike

key_facts: Madison Air acquires Airflow Technologies for $5.4B
